title: An all-inclusive approach: A universal protocol for the successful amplification of four genetic loci of all Onscidea
author: Dimitriou, Sfenthourakis

steps.title: Prepare PCR master mix
steps.instruction: In a sterile tube assemble a 20 µL reaction containing 0.1 µL Taq DNA polymerase (5 U/µL), 2.4 µL 25 mM MgCl₂, Taq buffer A to 1X final concentration, 0.6 µL 10 mM dNTP mix, and 0.6 µL of each primer (10 µM).

steps.title: Add DNA template
steps.instruction: Add DNA template to the master mix: use >2 ng for COI or 16S, >10 ng for 28S or NAK, but never exceed 100 ng; ensure DNA purity with A260/A280 > 1.5.

steps.title: Run PCR (standard profile)
steps.instruction: Program the thermocycler as follows: 94 °C 10 min (1 cycle); 94 °C 60 s, 55 °C 60 s, 72 °C 60 s (5 cycles); 94 °C 60 s, 50 °C 60 s, 72 °C 60 s (5 cycles); 94 °C 60 s, 47 °C 60 s, 72 °C 60 s (32 cycles); 94 °C 60 s, 42 °C 60 s, 72 °C 60 s (7 cycles); 72 °C 10 min (1 cycle); hold at 10 °C.

steps.title: Run PCR (stricter profile if needed)
steps.instruction: If nonspecific products appear, repeat PCR using this profile: 94 °C 10 min (1 cycle); 94 °C 60 s, 55 °C 60 s, 72 °C 60 s (10 cycles); 94 °C 60 s, 50 °C 60 s, 72 °C 60 s (10 cycles); 94 °C 60 s, 47 °C 60 s, 72 °C 60 s (30 cycles); 72 °C 10 min (1 cycle); hold at 10 °C.

steps.title: Visualize PCR products
steps.instruction: Run an aliquot of each PCR reaction on a standard agarose gel electrophoresis to confirm successful amplification.

steps.title: Purify PCR amplicons
steps.instruction: Purify the remaining PCR product using any commercial purification kit, following the manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Perform cycle sequencing
steps.instruction: Set up cycle‑sequencing reactions using the same primers as in the PCR, according to the sequencing kit protocol.
